newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya policemen arrested over student killings.
newsitem.headline: Kenya policemen arrested over student killings.

text.p: Two policemen were arrested after police shot dead two students at a Kenyan university, Nairobi newspapers on Thursday quoted Kenya's police chief as saying.
Police Commissioner Shedrach Kiruki said two policemen were arrested and firearms were taken for ballistic tests to identify which officer or officers fired the fatal shots on Wednesday.
Kiruki said police should have only had rubber bullets to disperse students at Kenyatta University on the outskirts of Nairobi in the second fatal shooting of students in two days.
A police spokesman was unavailable for comment on Thursday.

The two students died when police opened fire during a protest by Kenyatta University students against the killing on Tuesday of a student at Egerton University, Kenya's main agricultural school at Njoro 200 km (125 miles) northwest of Nairobi.
The East African Standard newspaper on Thursday quoted a policeman at the scene on Wednesday as saying police ran out of teargas to disperse students so had no alternative but to fire bullets.
A government statement issued on Wednesday said action would be taken against those reponsible for these "unfortunate acts".
It said police were called in after a report that Kenyatta University students were on the rampage, stoning cars, building barricades and lighting fires on a main road outside the campus.
It said students defied a police order to return to campus.
"Police shot in the air several times as a result of which the students ran back to the campus from where they engaged the police in a running battle," the government statement said.

"The police continued firing in the air as the skirmishes continued. The government is deeply saddened by the police action which led to the death of two students and serious injuries to three others," added the statement issued by Minister of State Jackson Kalweo.
Newspapers said one of the killed students was hit in the chest and the other in the hip. Bullets also hit the campus gates.
George Eshiwani, Kenyatta University's vice-chancellor, said he gave firm instructions police should not enter the campus on Wednesday because students were mourning their dead colleague.
"The students were not violent in any way. Why? Why had this to happen. You only needed to fire teargas and nothing more," he was quoted as telling a police officer after the shooting.
Following the killings Kenyatta University closed on Wednesday for Christmas instead of Friday as had been planned.
